Perl6 lexer incorrectly handles nested bracket delimiters

#### Description

The Perl6 lexer is not correctly parsing nested bracket delimiters in quoted strings and other constructs. When using mirrored characters like `()`, `[]`, `{}`, etc. as delimiters, the lexer appears to be swapping the opening and closing characters during the nesting level calculation, causing incorrect tokenization.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from pygments import highlight
from pygments.lexers import Perl6Lexer
from pygments.formatters import TerminalFormatter

code = '''
q{nested {brackets} here}
q[nested [brackets] here]
q(nested (parens) here)
'''

lexer = Perl6Lexer()
formatter = TerminalFormatter()
result = highlight(code, lexer, formatter)
print(result)
```

The lexer fails to properly handle the nested bracket structures, leading to incorrect syntax highlighting and potentially incomplete tokenization of the quoted strings.

#### Expected Behavior

The lexer should correctly identify matching opening and closing brackets while maintaining proper nesting levels, ensuring that quoted strings with nested delimiters are fully tokenized.
</issue>
